description.content:
Updates table and column definition metadata. Async-only - returns 202 with a storage job; poll it for completion. Backend DDL changes are not atomic across multiple column operations. If the async job fails after applying some changes, previously applied changes may remain applied. Re-read the table definition before retrying.

Initial response returns job details [JobResponse](#model-JobResponse). The result of the asynchronous job can be fetched via `/v2/storage/jobs/{id}`. When the job completes, final result is [TableCreateResponse](#model-TableCreateResponse).

 Parameters of job will be [TableDefinitionUpdateJobParams](#components-schemas-TableDefinitionUpdateJobParams).

The request does not contain any effective definition changes.

description.content:
Exchanges the physical storage of two tables in the same bucket. Async-only — returns 202 with a storage job; poll it for completion. Aliases are not transferred with table identity: each alias keeps pointing at the same physical position, so after the swap aliases expose the data of the other table. Both tables must live in the same bucket on the same backend connection.

Initial response returns job details [JobResponse](#model-JobResponse). The result of the asynchronous job can be fetched via `/v2/storage/jobs/{id}`. When the job completes, final result is [TableSwapResult](#model-TableSwapResult).

 Parameters of job will be [SwapJobParams](#components-schemas-SwapJobParams).

response.name: Job accepted; returns job details.
Validation error in the request payload, or the backend does not support swap (`storage.driver.unsupportedOperation`).
Access to one of the tables was denied.
Either table or its bucket was not found.

Operation not applicable: source and target are the same table (`storage.tables.sameTableSwap`), either side is an alias (`storage.tables.cannotSwapAlias`), or the tables live in different buckets (`storage.tables.crossBucketSwap`).
